observations: Photo 0: A used automatic transmission/gearbox assembly sitting on a dirty workshop floor, surrounded by other engine/transmission parts and scrap metal in the background.
Photo 0: Visible torque converter bell housing, flywheel area, and a fan clutch assembly; casing shows oxidation, grime and old oil residue consistent with a pulled used part.
Photo 1: Close-up of the gearbox casing showing a wiring harness connector with several loose/cut wires (red, blue, orange) twisted together, not connected to anything.
Photo 1: No part number, serial tag, or manufacturer plate is legible anywhere on the casing.
Photo 2: Another angle of a transmission case with hydraulic/vacuum lines and sensor connectors still attached, sitting among other stacked gearboxes in what looks like a parts yard.
No photo shows a test bench, a running engine, a VIN tag, or any plate confirming which exact vehicle model this unit came from.
Watermark 'NZ JAPANESE AUTOS' present on all photos, suggesting a parts dealer/stock photo source rather than a private seller's own unit necessarily matching the listing text.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the part/casting number or VIN tag on the gearbox casing
A video of the gearbox being tested (manual shift test or bench spin test for automatic)
Confirmation (photo) of which single model/year this specific unit in the photos belongs to
Photo showing the wiring harness connector fully intact and labeled
response.reason: The photos show a generic used transmission with no readable identifying tag, while the text vaguely covers three different vehicle models; without a part number or model-specific shot, even a worst-case price tier cannot be assigned since Corolla, Carry, and Hilux gearbox values differ substantially.
